comment: No source is published. Two pitch faults. The primary oscillator's frequency is 261.6256 times two to the power of (knob minus twelve plus twelve times the pitch voltage) over twelve, so the knob's own tooltip, which is configured with a semitone display base against 261.6256, reads exactly one octave above the note that is sounding. And the secondary oscillator in its Detune setting adds the pitch voltage to a semitone count without multiplying by twelve, so it rises one semitone per volt where the primary rises an octave; the two therefore part company as soon as a keyboard is patched. In the Free setting the secondary is instead a ratio of the primary's frequency, clamped to plus or minus twenty-four semitones. Both oscillator frequencies are finally clamped between 0.1Hz and 20000Hz. The pitch input is clamped to 0 to 5V before anything is done with it. The output passes through a sixteen-bit quantiser with a rand()-based dither term added before the plus or minus 5V clamp. The switch choices are the maker's own strings: LFO Mode is Pitch A/B, Pitch B and Alpha; LFO Waveform is Square/Random, Up/Down and Triangle/Sine; LFO Bank is Bank A (Sq/Up/Tri) and Bank B (Rnd/Down/Sin); Method is Phase, Multiply and Fade; Sync is Off and On; OSC B Mode is Free and Detune; OSC B Bank Copy is Sine to Sawtooth and Copy from A. Index order is not panel order for the inputs: the middle jack is input three, the modulation one.
